subject.title: Create Claw agent and root install record

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the experimental core `claws add` lifecycle that creates agents/workspaces and retains resumable root-install provenance, or should this capability remain outside core until a narrower owner-approved design exists?
rationale: The implementation adds a new public mutation workflow and authoritative shared-state lifecycle; source review can assess mechanics, but cannot decide whether this product boundary belongs in core.

options.title: Require explicit core sponsorship
options.body: Keep the stack open for maintainer-owned RFC/product approval, then integrate its prerequisite slices and this mutation slice in order.

options.title: Keep Claw packaging external
options.body: Do not merge the core lifecycle now; reuse ClawHub/plugins for independently distributable capability and reopen only for a demonstrated missing core API.

recommendation.title: Require explicit core sponsorship
recommendation.body: Keep the stack open for maintainer-owned RFC/product approval, then integrate its prerequisite slices and this mutation slice in order.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline explicitly routes the stacked Claws direction to this stakeholder; confidence remains low because supplied evidence has no direct ownership statement.
